issues.description: The solution implementation of Lecture declares attributes using snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods use camelCase attribute names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch will cause the class not to compile and contradicts the camelCase attribute names specified in the problem statement UML, blocking students from using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and method usages. For example, in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java (solution) rename the declared fields to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or update all constructor parameters and method references to use the declared snake_case names. Prefer matching the UML/camelCase names so the solution, template and problem statement are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect attributes using camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares differently named fields with underscores (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while its constructor and methods use the camelCase identifiers. This creates a naming mismatch across artifacts and an internal inconsistency in the solution that will confuse students mapping the UML/problem to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent naming convention for the Lecture attributes across all artifacts. Rename the solution fields to the camelCase names specified in the problem/UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or alternatively change all constructor and method references to match the underscore names — preferably adopt the camelCase names to align with the problem statement and Java conventions.
